notes:
The controller succeeded on about half of the practice runs. The left bin works most of the time; the right bin almost always fails.

Last results: 10/16 on a mixed set (seeds 100000–100015). On a later 20-seed set made up mostly of right-bin tasks, 7/20 succeeded and 1 dropped a cube. In the last two runs, which used only right-bin tasks, 0/10 succeeded both times. The final controller has not been run since its last edit, which switched the right-bin cube positions back to the version behind the 10/16 result.

How it works:
- Inverse kinematics: damped least-squares solver for the grasp site, holding the palm facing down. It has a posture bias and restarts from several seed poses if it gets stuck. The shoulder roll joint is capped based on shoulder pitch, because the upper arm otherwise hits the torso; that collision was blocking placements in the left bin.
- Grasp: the hand yaw is matched to a cube face, choosing the reachable option closest to a preferred direction. The hand moves over the cube at 0.93 m, comes straight down, and closes fully. The lift counts as a grasp only if the cube comes up with the hand; otherwise it retries.
- Placement: each episode picks two spots in the bin at startup, checked for reach. The left bin uses diagonal corners with the hand turned slightly (0.1 rad); the right bin uses two spots side by side along y. While carrying, the target corrects for the measured cube offset in the hand and turns the hand so the cube lines up with the bin. The cube is released about 7 mm above the rim, thumb first, then the fingers. This order stopped the first cube from being knocked 2–3 cm off target.

Known weaknesses:
1. Right bin, second cube: there is only about 1 cm of spare room. The second cube usually ends up resting raised (centre at about 0.845 m, above the 0.836 m rim) on the rim or the other cube. Moving the second cube's spot toward the first cube made no difference, so I'm not sure which of the two it is catching on. The far side of that bin is at the edge of the arm's reach, so diagonal spots were not possible there.
2. The left bin's second spot is slightly out of reach (about 5 mm error), which occasionally causes overlap.
3. One practice episode dropped a cube off the table during the initial grasp (seed 100025), and an earlier version knocked cubes off once (seed 100001).
4. I added a step that pushes the first cube toward the wall with the thumb, but it never triggered in testing, so it is unverified.
5. Placement depends on tight distances (2–4 mm), so it may not hold up if the physics or sensing differ.
